title: fix(plugin-detail): honour the `aria` bag the protocol declares on record blocks
body:
Part of objectui#9556

> ## ⚠️ EXHAUSTIVE CORRECTION — five sentences in this body are falsified by head `ec0ed06b5c9f540181d0f6829164e8a289fdf4b0`
>
> Written by the `domain:ui` seat at 2026-09-18T19:32Z, on findings from contract review `5734967234` and the round-two commit that followed it. ⭐ **This list is exhaustive by construction and ⛔ no sentence below was edited in place.** The last time this seat corrected a PR body it fixed two named sentences and left a third, which left repaired text sitting beside stale text and made the stale text look current. ⛔ Not repeated: the body stands as written, and every reading it gets wrong is listed here with its true value.
>
> **1. “It carries objectui#4663's read order (`??` between the canonical spelling and the legacy alias…)”** — no longer family-wide. The alias arm is now **opt-in**: `legacyLabelFold ? aria?.ariaLabel ?? aria?.label : aria?.ariaLabel`, default `false`. Measured by this seat on the head at 2026-09-18T19:31:34Z: exactly **two** renderers pass `legacyLabelFold: true`, `record-path.tsx` and `record-quick-actions.tsx`; ⭐ the five container renderers score **zero**, against a firing control (the probe finds the token wherever it exists).
>
> **2. “On the legacy `aria.label`: it stays a fold behind the canonical spelling”** — true only of those two blocks. At the reviewed head it had become true of **seven**, five of them for the first time, on blocks ⛔ no stored document ever reached. That was the contract review's Finding B; it is closed in the head above.
>
> **3. The Verification section's “395 files, 6658 tests, all green, at `84d8b7830`”** — two heads stale. The delivering dev reports 395 files / **6668** tests at `ec0ed06b5`, the ten new legs being the scoping pins. ⚠️ That is the **dev's** reading, relayed as such; ⛔ this seat did not re-run it.
>
> **4. The file-surface account omits the 12th file.** `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` is in this diff, under a **mid-task seat authorization** bounded to that one file and to its own `--claim-ledger` regeneration. Measured by this seat at 2026-09-18T18:45:30Z: the diff there is **one line, removed**. Full record in PR comment `5734749584` on this PR (`issue_url` ending `/issues/9935`, verified 2026-09-18T19:32:25Z).
>
> **5. objectui#4592 does ⛔ not close.** The gate's message says to close it once the ledger is empty; measured by this seat at 2026-09-18T18:45:41Z by brace-matching the `CLAIM_DEBT` block, **17 symbols remain across 5 packages** (`types` 12, `core` 2, `app-shell` 1, `plugin-view` 1, `react` 1).
>
>
> ⚠️ **This block's own correction, 2026-09-18T19:33Z.** Item 4 first cited PR comment `5734990763`. That id was **composed**, not read — `GET /issues/comments/5734990763` answers **404** (2026-09-18T19:32:25Z). The real record is `5734749584`, now above, fetched by id with its `issue_url` read in the same act. ⭐ Recorded rather than silently swapped: this seat's standing rule after two cross-card false citations today is that **every comment id it writes is fetched by id and its `issue_url` read in the same act**, and the rule was broken inside the very block written to correct other people's stale references.
>
> **6. ⚠️ Added 2026-09-18T19:55Z, and it falsifies this block's own “exhaustive by construction” claim.** “The new pin asserts through `getByRole(role, { name })`, never through the attribute.” ⛔ Literally false: contract review `5735439084` measured **six** attribute-level assertions in that pin — three `not.toHaveAttribute` in the no-aria cases, a `toHaveAttribute('aria-describedby', …)`, a `toHaveAttribute('role', 'region')` and a `getAttribute('aria-label')` — present at the first commit and unchanged at this head. ⭐ The clause a reader would act on still holds: every **positive name** assertion goes through the accessibility tree, so a name parked on a `generic` element does fail it. Body-only; ⛔ no commit needed.
>
> ⚠️ **And the word “exhaustive” was the seat's own claim, falsified by one sentence.** It was written to be falsifiable and it was falsified on the first hostile read — ⛔ which is the point of writing it that way, and ⛔ not a reason to stop. The lesson kept: a list is exhaustive only over the sentences someone actually re-read, so say which instrument read them.
>
> ⛔ Nothing else in this body was found stale, and ⛔ nothing in it was edited.


Clause-②: yes

The card measured `aria` as declared on six interfaces and read by one renderer,
and deliberately left the remedy open. Re-measured on this branch's base, the
shape is sharper than that and the two halves point to **opposite** exits.

## Re-measurement — every reading with its sha and time

Base `02bc27b084f8cf295f9173899cea2b55743c9442`, read `2026-09-18T17:58Z`.
Installed contract `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`. Re-checked against
`origin/main` `f5e2fcb4a16ae1b80b81db1dc890399c01a58c6a` at `2026-09-18T18:24:44Z`
before opening this PR (one neighbour landed under me, objectui#9927 — no file
overlap, and the `plugin-list` read point cited below still reads as quoted on
that head).

**The protocol declares `aria` on all six blocks.** `RecordDetailsProps`,
`RecordHighlightsProps`, `RecordRelatedListProps`, `RecordActivityProps`,
`RecordChatterProps` and `RecordPathProps` each carry it, and a document with
`aria: { ariaLabel: 'Account overview' }` on any of them `safeParse`s green. So
the declarations in `@object-ui/types` are FAITHFUL, not speculative — the card's
"retire the unread declarations" route would have to move `@objectstack/spec`
first, which is neither this repo nor this card's file surface.

**`record:path` was not the healthy row the card's table recorded.** It read
`(schema.aria as any)?.label` — the ONE spelling the shared ARIA shape refuses —
so the spec-valid `ariaLabel` it was credited with reading was exactly the value
it threw away. ⇒ **zero of the six spec-declared slots was honoured**, not one.

**`record:quick_actions` was not missing a props interface.** It declares
`RecordQuickActionsRendererProps` in its own module, `aria` included. The card's
instrument searched `packages/types/src` only, so a locally declared interface
was invisible to it. What IS true is narrower and sharper, and it inverts the
card's third route: the protocol declares **no** `aria` on
`RecordQuickActionsProps` and REFUSES the bag there with `unrecognized_keys`, so
that block's read is unreachable for any contract-valid document — and the
protocol's own refusal message names objectui's renderer as the side that moves
first, saying it will declare the key "when the two agree".

⇒ Under the maintainer's standing principle (spec declaration over
implementation over docs), an accepted-then-dropped key is an **implementation
gap**: the six renderers gain the read. ⛔ Nothing is narrowed on the consumer
side, ⛔ nothing is retired, and ⛔ no key the protocol refuses is mirrored onto a
published face.

## The widened scan, and its control

The card's instrument was a token-scoped grep over `packages/plugin-detail/src`.
Widened to the concept — any spelling of an aria bag read, repo-wide, including
casts and bracket forms, plus every props interface in the record-component
family — it returns sites the card did not name. ⭐ The first one is the card's
own corpus: `record-path`'s read is written `(schema.aria as any)?.label`, and
the `as any` is why a `aria?.label` pattern does not see it. The firing control
fires (the same instrument returns the two `record-*` read points it is known to
contain) and the absent-token control returns zero.

Sites outside the card's list, **reported whether or not they are changed here**:

| site | what it is | changed here |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `packages/types/src/layout.ts` `PageNodeSchema.aria` | spec-aligned, already widened by objectui#9092, read by `plugin-list` | no |
| `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` `NamedListView.aria` | a THIRD vocabulary (`label`/`describedBy`/`live`), folded to canonical at the ListView boundary | no |
| `packages/types/src/mobile.ts` `TouchInteraction` | flat `ariaLabel`/`ariaDescribedBy`/`role`, a different family | no |
| `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts` `DashboardConfig.aria` | already RETIRED to `z.never()` by objectui#5852 | no |
| `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` | `aria` off the spec's action input | no |
| `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx` `ariaAttrs()` | ⚠️ a fourth vocabulary — see below | no, out of surface |
| `plugin-view` / `app-shell` `ObjectView.tsx` | plumb `aria` down into the list schema | no |

⚠️ `ariaAttrs()` in `@object-ui/components` prefixes every key it is given with
`aria-` unless it already starts with `aria-` or is `role`. So on the four
`element:*` blocks that use it, the canonical `ariaLabel` becomes the invalid
attribute `aria-ariaLabel`, while the spelling the contract refuses (`label`)
becomes the working `aria-label` — the exact inversion this PR removes from
`record:path`, in another package. Out of this card's file surface; reported in
the structured report as a finding to file, ⛔ not fixed here.

## What changed

One shared read point, `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordComponentAria.ts`,
now serves the whole family. It carries objectui#4663's read order (`??` between
the canonical spelling and the legacy alias, `||` for the built-in default) and
takes each block's CURRENT role and name as its `defaultRole` / `defaultLabel`.

⭐ **It emits a role whenever it emits a name, and that is the load-bearing
part.** `aria-label` on a bare `div` reaches nobody — a `div` is `generic` and
browsers expose no accessible name on one. This family has already paid for that
once: `record:path`'s `aria-label="Alternative terminal stages"` sat on a `div`
and was inert rather than untranslated. Emitting the attribute alone would have
been a change CI calls green and a screen-reader user cannot hear. The fallback
role is `region`, matching `@object-ui/plugin-list`'s live read point
(`role={schema.aria?.role ?? 'region'}`), and an authored `aria.role` overrides
every default.

`RecordComponentAriaProps.ariaLabel` also stops narrowing the contract: it is
`string | I18nLabel`, the spec's inline locale map, and the renderers resolve it
with the spec's own `resolveI18nLabel`. This is a fourth site of objectui#9092's
Group A, missed there because it is reached through a shared interface rather
than restated inline.

**A document that declares no `aria` keeps the attributes it has today.**

## The four axes

**实际业务需求 — 实测, not "reads like it would be useful".** Who writes the key:
any author of a `record:*` block, and the contract accepts it today with a
success receipt. Who reads it: measured at zero for the six, by rendering them
rather than by grepping (a grep cannot answer this here — `SchemaRenderer` hands
a node's leftover keys to the component as props, so a renderer can consume a key
it never names). The user this serves is a screen-reader user on a record page,
which is why triage graded this p2 rather than p3: the failure is silent and the
author gets a receipt. ⚠️ Honest limit: the key is deliberately absent from the
registry `inputs` lists, so it is an escape hatch for a human author and not an
AI-authoring surface — this PR does not change that, and does not add it there.

**项目长远合理性.** Contract-first, no workaround. The protocol is the authority;
objectui was narrower than it on the read side (nothing honoured) and narrower on
the declaration side (`ariaLabel` as `string`). Catching up on both is the
direction the principle permits. The alternative — retiring six declarations
objectui does not own — would be objectui narrowing a protocol it mirrors, which
is the direction objectui#8980 ruled against on this very file.

**防 AI 写错,尤其是元数据.** This tightens rather than loosens. ⛔ No `??` alias is
introduced, ⛔ no lenient parse is added, ⛔ no key is declared that the runtime will
not honour — "声明即强制" is what the change delivers, for six blocks that
declared and did not honour. On the legacy `aria.label`: it stays a fold behind
the canonical spelling and is declared on NO authoring face, and — measured — the
contract REFUSES it, so it cannot mask a new authoring mistake; it can only serve
documents written before the shape closed.

**创业阶段不扩散需求.** No capability is invented and no declaration surface grows:
the keys already exist in the protocol, and this is implementation catching up to
them, which is the `implementation-first` disposition rather than an exception to
it. ⭐ It is also why `record:quick_actions` does **not** get a mirrored `aria`
declaration here — that would be new published surface for a key the contract
rejects. The one place the 立即退休 default would bite is the legacy `aria.label`
fold; I have **no named external-user evidence** either way, and retiring it
reverses objectui#4663's explicit, pinned decision on a published renderer, so it
is raised as an open question rather than taken in passing.

## Acceptance notes

- ⚠️ **On `record:activity` and `record:chatter` the authored name does not
  replace the panel's own.** Both mount a panel that already renders a named
  SECTION element with an accessible name, so an authored name lands on the outer container and the panel
  keeps its inner one — two nested named regions. Measured, and pinned as the
  SHIPPED behaviour rather than as the right answer. This is exactly the
  composition question the card raised; answering it the other way means plumbing
  into `RecordActivityTimeline` / `RecordChatterPanel`.
- The `record:related_list` "missing objectName" designer placeholder is
  deliberately left without the authored ARIA — it is a degenerate authoring
  state, not the block.
- ⛔ No `## Contract review` record here: that is the seat's, and a dev
  self-assessment is not one.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/ packages/types/` — 395 files,
  6658 tests, all green, at `84d8b7830`. Includes the two pre-existing ARIA pins
  (`record-path.containerLabel.test.tsx`, `record-quick-actions.ariaLabel.test.tsx`),
  both still green: the legacy fold is unchanged where it already existed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` and
  `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` — both exit 0, after building the
  dependency closure first (`--filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build`).
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` exit 0; `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`
  exit 0; `pnpm check:changeset-claims` exit 0.
- The new pin asserts through `getByRole(role, { name })`, never through the
  attribute, so a name parked on a `generic` element fails it.
- ⛔ No count or population in this PR or in the changeset is written down as a
  fact to be trusted: which blocks the contract declares `aria` on, which
  spellings the shared shape accepts, and whether `record:quick_actions` still
  refuses the bag are re-derived from the installed artifact on every run by
  `renderers/__tests__/recordComponentAria-9556.test.tsx`.
